result.text: Title: Storage management First, the order is read from the automatic order management system.
Then, it's checked if the first product from the order is in stock.
If it's in stock then it's withdrawn from the warehouse.
However, if it's not in stock then it's reordered from the wholesaler.
Note, that if it was necessary to wait more then 10 days for the arrival of the product then a delivery delay penalty is automatically demanded from the wholesaler.
After the ordered product has arrived it's registered in the stock management system.
Finally, it's checked if the whole order is ready for shipment.
If the order is ready for shipment, a courier is requested and the products are packed simultaneously and finally shipped.
If it isn't then the next product from the order is selected and the process starts again with checking if this order is in stock or not.

result.process_description:
Title: Storage management

First, the order is read from the automatic order management system.
Then, it's checked if the first product from the order is in stock.
If it's in stock then it's withdrawn from the warehouse.
However, if it's not in stock then it's reordered from the wholesaler.
Note, that if it was necessary to wait more then 10 days for the arrival of the  product then a delivery delay penalty is automatically demanded from the wholesaler.
After the ordered product has arrived it's registered in the stock management system.
Finally, it's checked if the whole order is ready for shipment.
If the order is ready for shipment, a courier is requested and the products are packed simultaneously and finally shipped.
If it isn't then the next product from the order is selected and the process starts again with checking if this order is in stock or not.

result.rule: When the description says an external party will arrive at a time that is not fixed in advance, and the next activity can only start after that arrival: Model the waiting period as an intermediate catch event placed between the preceding activity and the next activity, not as a task. Do not represent the wait as an activity that performs the work itself.

When the description says that, after an external party reports that a requested outcome is delayed, the process notifies a human user of the delay and asks the user to check again, and only afterwards the process waits for the outcome to arrive so it can be shown to that user: Model the notification of the delay to the user as its own task (a user task or manual task that the process performs for the user), placed on the sequence flow right after the event that reports the delay and before the intermediate catch event that waits for the outcome. Do not omit the notification, and do not let the wait event stand in for it, because the wait event only records that the outcome has arrived.

When the description says a team sends a request to outside actors and then takes in their returned items as work the team carries out, and no stated occurrence is one the process must wait for before it can continue: Model the taking-in of the returned items as a task placed on the sequence flow after the request task and before the next step that uses them. Do not model it as an intermediate catch event. Reserve an intermediate catch event for an occurrence the process must wait for before it can continue.

When the description states that the actor performs an outward action of their own, such as placing an order with one or more outside suppliers, and then says the result is still in progress or pending while other work goes on: Model the actor's outward action as its own task, named with a verb and the object that is placed or sent, and place it on the sequence flow before the waiting step. Model the waiting as a separate intermediate catch event that follows that task, and name the catch event after the occurrence the process awaits (for example, receipt of the outcome), not after the pending state. Keep any other work that proceeds during the wait on its own branch, and do not replace the action task with the catch event.
